GRACE achieves consistently positive uncertainty-localisation error correlations, with mean Pearson r ranging from approximately 0.37 under compression to 0.65 under resize-crop, and around 0.56 under blur.
In contrast, EMM remains close to zero across most perturbations, while ModelNet is frequently negatively correlated.

experiments.summary: COCO represents the largest GRACE overhead at 8.01 ± 4.76ms, but this remains substantially below ModelNet and MetaDetect.

evidence.quote: COCO represents the largest GRACE overhead at 8.01 ± 4.76ms, but this remains substantially below ModelNet and MetaDetect.
Overall, GRACE introduces a small inference overhead comparable to the lightweight EMM baseline, while remaining considerably more efficient than ModelNet and MetaDetect across all four datasets.

limitations.summary: D A DDITIONAL D ISCUSSION The relative improvement provided by GRACE varies across datasets, with TT100K representing the clearest case in which EMM remains particularly competitive.
items: D A DDITIONAL D ISCUSSION The relative improvement provided by GRACE varies across datasets, with TT100K representing the clearest case in which EMM remains particularly competitive.

Rather than indicating a failure of the proposed uncertainty-guidance mechanism, this result suggests that the frozen detector representations on TT100K already encode a comparatively strong localisation-reliability signal, reducing the additional benefit available from curriculum-based refinement.
However, GRACE still outperforms EMM on this dataset, showing the additional benefit of the saliency calibration and the curriculum training.
